parsed.why: No criminalisation and anti-discrimination/hate-crime law, but police assault on LGBT people went unsanctioned, an LGBT centre closed after 20+ unsanctioned attacks, and pride violence plus rule-of-law weakness show societal hostility with thin recourse.

Currently permissive with hate-crime aggravation, protected facility access and no trans-specific restriction; but parliament's first-reading rollback of self-ID signals a hostile trajectory, and recourse/court posture on trans issues is now contested.

Decriminalised, gender-identity discrimination criminalised, hate-crime recording rising but enforced by functioning police; no documented trans-specific violence, border friction or facility rule. Resident healthcare gaps and legacy sterilisation are climate negatives only.

Same-sex conduct criminalised with lashes/up to eight years, no gender-identity protection, state rejects UN recommendations, pervasive stigma and no recourse; but no trans-specific provision, little enforcement after 2015, and no documented trans targeting.

Morality-law criminalisation with recent documented enforcement and imprisonment (Dec 2024), no protections, no gender-marker change, no LGBTIQ organisation and impunity; episodic rather than systematic policing, but no recourse if a trans visitor is outed.
